notes.summary: Raw all-support envelope calculus and actual graded ideals; geometric positivity is equivalent to continuity of the raw envelope.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs raw C=D envelopes, lower semicontinuity, regularization iff continuity, nonexpansiveness, integrally closed all-support J_k ideals, the factorial profile formula, and exact one-factor primary-gauge covariance. No increasing-limit positivity is assumed.
notes.text:
Use the entire qualified G331, including its mandatory annotation, ledger and scope. For an excellent local ring R, work with its reduction and a proper maximal-primary gauge a. The compact Hausdorff section X consists of ALL centred real semivaluations with v(a)=1, retaining nonminimal prime supports. The independent geometric core evaluates actual negative effective real Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups, with nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve. C is its finite continuous uniform closure, and D its actual decreasing-C-net completion, including bottom. G331 supplies its ideal comparison and positive full-fibre descent, but no envelope theorem.

For finite continuous phi, let p_C and p_D be the pointwise suprema of their respective minorants. Negative primary constants bound both below. If u=inf_i g_i is an admissible D-function, the directed open sets {g_i<phi+epsilon} cover X. Compactness selects one index globally, and g_i-epsilon is an admissible C-function at least u-epsilon. Thus p_C=p_D=p. It is finite, bounded and lower semicontinuous.

If p is continuous, the open sets {g>p-epsilon}, over C-minorants, cover X. A finite maximum approximates p uniformly from below, so p belongs to C. Conversely membership in D makes p upper semicontinuous, hence continuous. A greatest D-minorant therefore exists exactly when p is continuous. For p*(x)=inf_{open U containing x}sup_U p, continuity of phi gives p<=p*<=min(phi,0). If p* belongs to D, it is an admissible competitor and forces p*=p. Consequently geometric regularization is equivalent to raw continuity. Downward shifts of competitors prove ||P phi-P psi||<=||phi-psi||.

Define the ACTUAL ideal J_k(phi)={f in R:v(f)>=-k phi(v) for EVERY v in X}. The semivaluation axioms make it an ideal. If M>=max(0,-min phi), it contains a^ceil(kM), with a usable when that exponent is zero. It is proper primary when phi is negative somewhere, and the unit ideal when phi>=0 everywhere. It is integrally closed: a violation of the inequality in a monic ideal-integrality equation would make the leading power of f the unique finite least-valued term. Passing to the quotient by the semivaluation support justifies this argument on nonminimal supports too. Noetherianity gives finite generation of each ideal, not of the graded algebra.

The inclusions J_k J_l subset J_(k+l) and J_k^l subset J_(kl) show that -v(J_(n!))/(n!) increases. Its supremum is p. Indeed approximate any C-minorant rationally by a single primary profile, then subtract a small positive rational primary constant by multiplying suitable ideal powers after synchronizing denominators. The resulting admissible rational profile lies arbitrarily close below the original minorant. Its ideal is contained in the corresponding J_k, and k divides every sufficiently large factorial. This proves the formula on ALL supports without granting positivity of its increasing limit.

For another primary gauge b, put d(v)=v(b)>0 and H(v)=v/d(v). Both d and 1/d are bounded continuous. Transport functions AND obstacles by phi_b(Hv)=phi_a(v)/d(v). The granted order bijections give P_b(phi_b)(Hv)=P_a(phi_a)(v)/d(v), with exactly one homogeneous factor. The defining J_k inequalities divide by that same d, so the ideals are literally unchanged. Bounded regularization transports because 1/d is continuous; the cocycle follows by cancellation of successive denominators.

Nilpotents are invisible. Dimension-zero local reduction has empty boundary and its unique empty envelope. Units give zero models; unit and zero ideals have no level-one section. Lower-dimensional centres, nonminimal supports, mixed zero and partial bottom remain function and conductor data. Nonprimary gauges give partial sections and are outside these compact primary assertions.

notes.summary: Decreasing D-net closure on every excellent reduced germ, proved before applying the energy criterion.
notes.detailedSummary: Normal zero dichotomy and strict-majorant insertion construct an actual decreasing C representation. Full normalization descent handles arbitrary reduced germs. E350 then supplies the decreasing energy criterion without an additional membership hypothesis; no increasing closure is proved.
notes.text:
Use G331 and n1. Suppose u_i in D decreases, and set u=inf_i u_i. On an excellent normal local domain, G331's normal zero dichotomy says that a D-function vanishing anywhere is identically zero. If u vanishes at a point, all u_i vanish there, so u=0. Otherwise choose a nonzero u_i0. Compact upper semicontinuity gives u_i0<=-c for a finite c>0, including bottom. Hence u<=-c.

For every finite continuous F>u there is q in C with u<q<F. The directed open sets {u_i<F} cover X; choose a common tail index i>=i0. An ACTUAL C-representation g_alpha decreasing to u_i has one term g satisfying g<F and g<-c/2 throughout X, by compact directed covers. With m=min(F-g)>0, choose 0<b<1 such that b||g||<m/2. Then q=(1-b)g belongs to C, stays below F, and exceeds u at finite points by at least bc/2. At bottom points it is finite and also exceeds u. No positive constant was added to C.

All strict C-majorants of u contain zero and are downward directed: apply insertion to the continuous minimum of two majorants, which need not itself be psh. Their infimum is u. For x and finite t>u(x), choose u(x)<ell<t and a neighbourhood where u<ell. A compact-Hausdorff cutoff interpolates between ell at x and a global strict upper bound outside, producing continuous F>u with F(x)<t. At bottom choose any finite ell<t. Insertion supplies a majorant whose value at x is below t. Reverse pointwise order gives an ACTUAL decreasing C-net with infimum u.

For finitely many semilocal normal centres take finite products of the index sets. For arbitrary excellent reduced R, pull the net back to its finite normalization S. The centrewise infima belong to D_S by this construction. Their tuple is constant on EVERY full restriction fibre, since each pulled-back term is. G331's positive D-descent puts its descent, exactly u, in D_R. This includes internal and conductor-infinite fibres; the empty case is immediate.

Thus D is closed under nonempty decreasing D-nets on every excellent reduced germ. No finite-minimum, nondirected-infimum, increasing-limit or arbitrary nested-net flattening theorem is asserted.

Only after membership is proved use qualified E350: for a decreasing E1-net, its infimum belongs to D and is in E1 iff sup_i F_infinity(u_i^[n]) is finite. The qualified weak mixed-measure and capacity convergence then apply. Energy is E=-F_infinity/n. Lower-dimensional centres retain their class and fibre constraints despite zero ambient top-degree contribution. This criterion does not manufacture membership of an increasing obstacle supremum.

notes.summary: Every finite chosen primary model of an excellent normal surface has a regular refinement which is itself an actual primary blowup.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks the exact current Lipman hypotheses, connected fibre, actual Cartier degree matrix, reference-vector negative definiteness, principal inverse positivity and strict integral boundary. Full-fibre ampleness and the identical punctured graph prove actual Bl_I realization in every characteristic and mixed characteristic.
notes.text:
Let R be an excellent NORMAL local domain of dimension two, with arbitrary residue field and characteristic, including mixed characteristic. Use G331 for the actual primary-model system. Given finitely many proper primary ideals, including a, their product blowup dominates the individual blowups. It is integral projective and is an isomorphism off the closed point. Normalize it; excellence makes normalization finite. The normal surface has finitely many singular points, because excellence makes its nonregular locus closed and normality puts it in codimension at least two. The local completions are normal. The complete CURRENT Stacks 54.14.5 (0BGP), condition (4) implying (3), therefore gives a resolution by normalized blowups. The complete 0BGJ section supplies the normalized-blowup construction. Finite normalization and blowups preserve projectivity here. The centres lie over the closed point. We obtain regular integral projective T, isomorphic over the punctured spectrum, principalizing every chosen ideal. No SNC claim is needed.

Current Stacks 0AY8, Lemma37.53.6, applies: the morphism is proper, R integral normal, T reduced and generically dominating, and generic H0 equals Frac(R). Thus Gamma(T,O_T)=R and its fibres are geometrically connected. Regular local rings are factorial, so the exceptional irreducible curves E_i are Cartier. They are proper integral residue-field curves. The invertible primary ideal a O_T has effective Cartier divisor E_a=sum b_i E_i, with integers b_i>0, supported on the entire closed fibre. There are no isolated fibre points because a Cartier divisor on this regular surface has pure codimension one.

Set M_ij=deg_k(O_T(E_j)|E_i), k=R/m. This ACTUAL degree matrix is symmetric; off-diagonal entries are sums of local intersection lengths times actual residue degrees and are nonnegative. The fibre's connectedness makes the intersection graph connected. The bundle O_T(-E_a) is the pullback of the ample tautological bundle on Bl_a R, giving M b<=0. At least one entry is strict. Indeed Bl_a has a fibre curve: otherwise this projective birational morphism would be quasi-finite and finite, hence an isomorphism over normal R. Then a would be invertible and principal, contradicting the principal ideal theorem for a proper primary ideal in dimension two. Some T-curve dominates that fibre curve, where the ample bundle has positive degree.

Put A=-M. For t_i=b_i z_i, direct expansion gives

t^T A t = sum_i (A b)_i b_i z_i^2 + sum_{i<j}(-A_ij)b_i b_j(z_i-z_j)^2.

Every term is nonnegative. Vanishing forces all z_i equal along the connected graph and zero at a strict coordinate. Thus A is positive definite. Every principal submatrix A_J is positive definite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries, and its inverse is entrywise nonnegative. To prove this, solve A_J x=y>=0 and write x=x_+-x_- with disjoint nonnegative parts. If x_- is nonzero, x_-^T y=x_-^T A_J x_+-x_-^T A_J x_-<0, a contradiction. Moreover A^-1 1 is strictly positive: a zero coordinate of a nonnegative solution would give the corresponding row value <=0. Since M is integral, this vector is rational. Clear denominators to obtain integers d_i>0 with M d<0.

For D0=sum d_i E_i, O_T(-D0) has positive degree on every closed-fibre integral curve. The complete Stacks0B5Y criterion applies to the ENTIRE proper fibre of dimension at most one, including nonreduced structure and imperfect residue field, and makes the restriction ample. CURRENT30.21.4 (0D2N) gives relative ampleness near m, hence on the whole local base. Ordinary Serre generation/coherence and relative very ampleness give a large N such that L^N, L=O_T(-D0), is generated and defines a closed immersion by finitely many sections.

Because Gamma O_T=R and L^N is an actual subsheaf of O_T, I=Gamma(T,L^N) is a finite ideal of R. It is unit off m and proper, since it vanishes on the exceptional boundary. Therefore it is primary and I O_T=L^N. Choose ideal generators containing the sections defining the immersion. Enlarging the list preserves a closed immersion: on the opens where an original section is nonzero it is the graph of the additional ratios, and properness closes the image. In the same projective space, T and Bl_I R are integral closed subschemes agreeing with the same punctured graph. Their prime ideals on each affine chart are determined by vanishing on that dense graph. Both are its scheme-theoretic closure. Thus T is ACTUALLY Bl_I R. The same proof applies to every regular common refinement obtained from finitely chosen primary models. No arbitrary proper-model cofinality is asserted.

Recursive published background is disclosed: 0BGP uses the preceding surface blowup/descent lemmas and Lipman; 0AY8 uses Stein factorization; 0B5Y uses finite-surjective ampleness descent; 0D2N uses formal functions and fibre section lifting. Serre generation and regular-local factoriality are ordinary published background. Complete immediate bound units were read, but deeper historical bodies are not claimed freshly recursively proved.

notes.summary: Full surface competitor domination and the greatest finite signed-profile envelope from a nef polytope.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual primary common refinement, nef Cartier pushforward, exceptional negativity and all-support evaluations dominate every core, C and bounded D competitor. Unbounded competitors clamp. Coordinate-max stability supplies the greatest feasible vector and the full envelope.
notes.text:
Use G331, n1 and n3. Fix a regular ACTUAL primary surface model T with E_a=sum b_i E_i. A core competitor is represented by a negative effective real curve-nef Cartier divisor D' on another actual primary model. A regular common refinement T' is itself an actual primary blowup by n3. Pullback preserves effectivity and curve-nefness. Write mu:T'->T and D=mu_*D'. This is a negative exceptional real Cartier divisor on regular T.

For each E_i, mu*E_i is a nonnegative sum of proper curves contracted to R. Actual degree projection gives D.E_i=D'.mu*E_i>=0. Explicitly, a component C' mapping to a point has degree zero for a pulled-back bundle, while a curve image gives its degree multiplied by the function-field degree, precisely the coefficient of mu_*C'. Expand D' and use symmetry of actual surface Cartier intersections. This is supported divisor-cycle projection and the ordinary degree rule, as in the complete Stacks0AYA units, before taking a Chow quotient. Hence D is nef over R.

F=D'-mu*D is supported only on mu-exceptional curves, since a proper birational map of normal surfaces is an isomorphism at generic codimension-one points. For each such curve C, mu*D.C=0, so F.C=D'.C>=0. The relevant principal intersection submatrix has negative inverse by n3. If f is the coefficient vector of F, M_J f>=0 implies f<=0. Therefore F is ACTUALLY negative effective. Evaluation gives h_D'<=h_D on EVERY semivaluation support. First pass to Frac(R/p), where p is the support, and lift its valuation-ring morphism to the proper model from its generic point in the punctured spectrum. Effective exceptional local equations have nonnegative finite value. No map from Frac(R) to Frac(R/p) is presumed. The exact projected coefficients are c_i=b_i h_D'(nu_i), nu_i=ord_Ei/b_i.

For h in C, choose core approximants converging uniformly to h. Their projected coefficients converge to c_i=b_i h(nu_i). Negativity and M c>=0 survive. At a valued centre, v(E_i) is finite and nonnegative, zero if the centre is off E_i, and sum b_i v(E_i)=v(a)=1. Thus projected evaluations converge uniformly and h<=sum c_i v(E_i). The limit is a genuine negative effective nef real Cartier divisor on the actual primary T.

For bounded h in D, use its SPECIFIED actual C-net. Its finitely many coefficients decrease to b_i h(nu_i), remain finite, and the finite evaluation sum commutes with the limit. The resulting nef model function dominates h. An unbounded competitor below f>=-B can be replaced by max(h,-B): the actual representation max(g_alpha,-B) proves membership in bounded D, and this clamp remains below f.

Let f be a finite SIGNED linear combination of finitely many primary ideal profiles and constants. Construct T by n3 for those ideals and a. Its actual Cartier representation gives f(v)=sum_i b_i f(nu_i)v(E_i) on ALL supports. Choose B>0 with f>=-B. The compact polytope

-B b_i <= c_i <= min(0,b_i f(nu_i)), with M c>=0,

is nonempty because -B b is feasible. It is stable under coordinatewise maximum: in row i choose the vector attaining the maximum ith coordinate; every other coordinate only increases and every off-diagonal entry is nonnegative. Choose a maximizer of each coordinate and take their finite maximum. This produces a greatest vector c*.

The actual negative effective nef Cartier divisor sum c*_i E_i on T evaluates to H* in the geometric core. Since all v(E_i)>=0, H*<=f everywhere. Every D-minorant, after clamping and projection, has a feasible coefficient vector and is at most H*. Hence H* is the FULL geometric envelope, rather than an envelope only among competitors on T.

Neither an SNC premise nor a singular retraction is used. The decisive all-support dominance is actual Cartier negativity of F on a common actual primary regular model. notes.summary: Continuous and extended USC geometric envelopes on every excellent normal surface, with full decreasing-obstacle net stability.
notes.detailedSummary: Signed ideal density and nonexpansiveness give every finite continuous obstacle. One actual continuous-majorant net gives bounded-above extended USC envelopes. Existing-D energy and quasicontinuity apply only afterwards; exact gauge transport is preserved.
notes.text:
Use G331, E350 and n1--n4. G331's signed ideal-difference lattice is uniformly dense in all real continuous functions on the FULL compact section. Approximate a finite continuous obstacle phi on an excellent normal surface uniformly by signed finite ideal combinations f_j. N4 puts their FULL envelopes in C. N1's raw nonexpansive estimate makes these converge uniformly to the raw envelope of phi. Closedness of C proves P(phi) in C, so it is the actual greatest D-minorant. This establishes continuous envelopes for EVERY excellent normal local surface, in arbitrary characteristic and residue field, including mixed characteristic. Only finitely chosen primary models are used.

The following extension works on ANY germ already proved to have the continuous-envelope property. For extended USC phi:X->[-infinity,M], M finite, take all finite continuous strict majorants F. This family is nonempty, closed under finite minimum and has infimum phi. For x and finite t>phi(x), choose phi(x)<ell<t, a cutoff supported in {phi<ell} equal to one at x, and M'>max(M,ell). Then F=chi ell+(1-chi)M' is strictly above phi and F(x)<t, including at bottom. The positive envelopes P(F) form ONE actual decreasing C-net. Its infimum belongs to D by definition, lies below phi and dominates every D-minorant of phi. It is therefore the greatest geometric envelope. No flattening or increasing completion is involved.

For ANY decreasing net of bounded-above USC obstacles phi_i with limit phi, restrict to a tail bounded above by a finite constant. N2 puts inf_i P(phi_i) in D. For every finite continuous F>phi, the directed open sets {phi_i<F} cover compact X, so one index works globally. Hence inf_i P(phi_i)<=P(F). Taking the infimum over F and combining with the opposite order inequality proves P(phi)=inf_i P(phi_i). This is full decreasing-USC-obstacle net stability.

Finite continuous outputs are bounded continuous geometric psh. General bounded-above USC outputs are USC with an actual decreasing C representation. If the obstacle is bounded below, its envelope is bounded D, hence E1. Qualified E350 then supplies open-exception quasicontinuity and the geometric energy/product calculus. For a general extended obstacle, E1 membership is equivalent to a uniform diagonal F_infinity bound on the decreasing P(F) net, by n2 and E350. Energy is E=-F/n. No uniqueness, strict concavity or capacity-a.e. replacement of exact obstacle order is inferred.

Primary-gauge covariance is exactly n1's single homogeneous factor, including extended outputs and stability. Greatestness gives idempotence on D; zero and bottom remain. Nonnormal germs require full conductor compatibility. This completes the NORMAL surface sector, not the entire arbitrary-dimensional original.

notes.summary: Exact BFJ smooth envelope specialization at affine closed algebraically closed characteristic-zero germs only.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs determining nef envelopes using substantive closed-face continuity, all retractions and the complete fixed-complex 3.18/3.22 uniform ideal estimate, then dense signed profiles. No higher-dimensional arbitrary-characteristic or singular multiplier transfer is made.
notes.text:
Use qualified G331 and n1, and n5's general USC extension after continuous envelopes are established. The new published application is Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, ONLY at a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension at least two. Complete immediate Setting, coefficient topology, simple modifications and retractions, Definitions2.1/2.5/2.8, Proposition2.7, substantive CLOSED-simplex Proposition3.11, and ENTIRE Section3.5 including3.18 and the full3.22 proof were read. Recursive Hironaka principalization, DEL/Lazarsfeld multiplier subadditivity, smooth Izumi and ELS approximation are disclosed published background, not transferred to singular or arbitrary-characteristic germs.

For a finite continuous obstacle h determined on one simple-modification complex, take the coefficient supremum W of nef divisors below Z(h). Clamp competitors above the nef constant -M, with -M<=h. Their finite maxima form a coefficientwise bounded increasing net; the published nef cone is weak closed and max-stable, so W is nef. Proposition3.11 gives its function g, continuous on each CLOSED simplex, with canonical extension g(v)=inf_pi g(r_pi v). Coefficient bounds and rational divisorial density give -M<=g<=0 on all faces, then ALL semivaluations. On the determining complex g<=h, and2.7 gives g(v)<=g(r_pi v)<=h(v). Every D-minorant of h has, by G331, BFJ coefficients below W, and therefore lies below g on closed faces and through all retractions. Bottom is separate.

The complete published3.18(iii) estimate for this determining envelope, with k=j+C, is W_j<=W<=j/(j+C) W_j, where W_j=Z(L^infinity(jW))/j. C is finite and depends on the FIXED complex, not on globally bounded thinness. The entire proof uses3.22 to recover W from those ideals, smooth multiplier subadditivity, and thinness versus strict negativity on that complex. The unused3.18(iv) and its proof were read too.

For W=0 use the unit ideal. Otherwise L^infinity(jW) contains a completed maximal-ideal power from W>=-M and is proper because W has a negative coefficient. G331 contracts it exactly to R, preserving its primary profile g_j on ALL supports. Extend coefficient inequalities by actual closed-face continuity and every retraction. They give g_j<=g and g_j>=(1+C/j)g, hence 0<=g-g_j<=MC/j uniformly on the FULL boundary. Thus g belongs to C before it is used as the positive greatest envelope.

For arbitrary finite continuous phi, approximate it uniformly by signed rational primary profiles. Principalize their finitely many ideals on a common simple modification in the exact published smooth range, making each obstacle determined on a complex. N1's nonexpansive estimate and closedness of C give P(phi) in C. This is the published determining nef envelope and its continuous-obstacle uniform extension, on every support. N5 supplies extended USC envelopes and full decreasing-obstacle stability in this same range. Gauge changes are n1; DVR and empty cases are direct in n9.

Closed-face continuity is substantive: finite convexity alone does not give continuity on a closed simplex's boundary. All retractions, rather than only divisorial values, are required. No singular multiplier estimate or arbitrary-characteristic higher-dimensional smooth theorem follows. Dimension two has the separate characteristic-free proof n3--n5.

notes.summary: Normal-target finite dominating covers transfer envelopes, including nonflat covers; full-fibre maxima preserve C and D.
notes.detailedSummary: Coefficient norm and Galois orbit maxima work on all supports. Positive full-fibre averages prove source envelopes fibre constant. Transfers continuous and USC envelopes from proved source sectors, without assuming every normal germ has a suitable cover or inventing vertical degrees.
notes.text:
Use G331 and n1--n6. Let A be an excellent normal local domain and B a finite reduced injection whose EVERY minimal component dominates A. Retain all marked semilocal centres and all supports. G331's coefficient norm construction gives a positive normalized trace for a dominating domain source, with a finite positive weight at EVERY point of the FULL restriction fibre. For several dominating components sum their generic-degree traces and divide by the sum of their degrees. This continuous operator preserves C and D and is a left inverse to pullback. No degree is fabricated for vertical components, and no flat or defectless ramification formula is assumed.

There is also an explicit fibre-maximum construction. For a component B/P choose a finite normal field extension M/K containing its field and every embedding image, including inseparability. Let E be A's finite integral closure in M, G=Aut_K(M), and q=[M:K]/|G|. At any base semivaluation and any lift w, the coefficient norm on E has measure q sum_(sigma in G) delta_(w composed with sigma). This follows from norm factorization, quotient-support Gauss coefficient minima and signed ideal density, as proved inside G331. Independence of this measure and its full-fibre support imply that G is transitive on the ENTIRE E/A fibre, including nonminimal supports.

For H in C_B, restrict to B/P, pull back to E and take the finite maximum of its G-translates. It lies in C_E and is fibre constant over A. Positive descent produces a C_A function equal to the maximum of H on that component's full fibre. Finite maximum over all dominating components gives MH(v)=max_(rho(w)=v)H(w) in C_A. For H in D_B use its actual decreasing C-net. Since each fibre is finite, directed simultaneous strict tests prove max_w inf_alpha H_alpha(w)=inf_alpha max_w H_alpha(w), including bottom. Thus MH belongs to D_A by an actual C representation.

For K=C or D and a finite bounded obstacle f, H<=rho*f implies MH<=f and H<=rho*(MH). Pullback gives the reverse inequality between competitor suprema. Therefore unrestricted raw envelopes satisfy P_B^K(rho*f)=rho*P_A^K(f) on all supports, even before output regularity is known.

Suppose each marked source centre has the continuous-envelope property, established by n5 for normal surfaces or n6 in the exact smooth BFJ range. For continuous f set U=P_B(rho*f) in C_B. Its positive normalized average p belongs to C_A and is below f. Every target D-minorant pulls back below U and hence lies below p. Also rho*p is a source minorant, so rho*p<=U. On a fibre, p is a positive weighted average of the finite U(w) and is no greater than any one of them. All values therefore equal the average. Thus rho*p=U and p is the greatest continuous geometric envelope. No extended-bottom average is used to force constancy. For bounded-above USC obstacles use ONE net of continuous strict majorants as in n5; its pullback infimum dominates every source minorant, proving source greatestness and commutation. The gauge, regularity and decreasing-net conclusions follow.

A concrete NONFLAT cover is A=k[U,V,W]_(m)/(UW-V^2) inside B=k[x,y]_(x,y), with U=x^2,V=xy,W=y^2. A is normal by the parity-lattice intersection argument of n10. B is finite of generic degree two with one marked centre. Its closed fibre has basis 1,x,y because mB=(x,y)^2, so has length three; a finite flat rank-two algebra would have fibre dimension two. The cover is not flat but satisfies the theorem. It works in every characteristic by the normal surface theorem. Adding smooth variables gives higher-dimensional characteristic-zero examples by n6.

These are proved finite-cover sectors, not a theorem that every excellent normal germ has a good cover. The maximum argument is characteristic-independent; higher-dimensional source regularity remains an explicit hypothesis. Nonnormal targets and vertical components are outside it.

notes.summary: Sharp full conductor criterion and an all-characteristic nonnormal obstacle with no maximal geometric minorant.
notes.detailedSummary: A primary conductor mask proves dense finite-conductor equality. Positive regularization is equivalent to continuous, full-fibre-constant separated raw envelope. The strictly negative double-plane example does not resolve the normal higher-dimensional residual.
notes.text:
Use G331, n1, n5 and n7. Let S be the finite normalization of excellent reduced R, split into ALL marked normal centres, with full compact quotient rho. Finite conductor value gives singleton fibres; infinite value gives exactly restriction fibres over the conductor quotient, including internal fibres of a single centre. Positive C/D descent is full-fibre constancy. Therefore the downstairs raw envelope pulls back to the supremum of upstairs minorants constant on EVERY fibre, not automatically to the unrestricted envelope.

For finite continuous phi, with unrestricted upstairs raw envelope p_S, the exact criterion is: p_R* belongs to D_R iff p_S is continuous AND constant on every full fibre. First prove equality of constrained and unrestricted raw suprema at finite conductor value. Choose B>0 with -B<=phi and clamp an upstairs C-minorant g into [-B,0]. The ACTUAL primary ideal K_N=c+a^N gives b_N=-(B/N)v(K_N), between -B and zero and equal to -B at conductor-infinite points. Then max(g+rho*b_N,-B) belongs to C_S, lies below rho*phi and is fibre constant: it equals -B on the entire nontrivial-fibre stratum. It descends positively. At finite conductor value the mask tends to zero, proving equality there.

This locus is dense in each normal centre. The conductor has a regular element; centred fraction-field divisorial valuations have finite value on it, and G331 proves divisorial density on the all-support topology. If p_R* belongs to D, n1 makes p_R continuous. Its continuous pullback u<=p_S agrees with p_S on this dense locus. A net approaching any point and lower semicontinuity of p_S give p_S<=u. Hence equality everywhere proves necessity. Conversely continuous p_S belongs to C_S by n1 and descends positively when fibre constant, yielding the greatest downstairs envelope. For ANY field take R=k[x,y,z]_(m)/(xy), with normalization A times B, A=k[x,z]_(x,z), B=k[y,z]_(y,z). At column 0<=x<r+s, minimizing the admissible i gives the smallest y as r+s-x+(j-1)max(0,s-x). Summing produces (r+s)(r+s+1)/2+(j-1)s(s+1)/2, the stated formula. Second take R=k[X,Y,Z]_(m)/(XY-Z^2)=k[s^2,st,t^2]_(m), over ANY field. For M={(i,j) in Z^2:i+j even}, its affine ring is k[M] intersect k[s,t] in k(s,t).
